statement: Every interior angle of a regular polygon measures 150 degrees. How many sides does it have?

choices.misconception: I divided 1500 by 150 without first working out how many angles there were.
I read the 150 as a count of something and divided 2250 by 150 to get a side count.
I used the exterior angle but subtracted 150 from 180 and then divided 720 rather than 360 by it.
I divided 180 by 150 and then multiplied by 25, chasing a number rather than a reason.

hints: Exterior angles are easier here than interior ones.
Each exterior angle is 180 minus the interior angle. The exterior angles of any polygon add to 360, so divide 360 by one of them.
Each exterior angle is 180 - 150 = 30 degrees. The exterior angles total 360, and 360 / 30 gives the number of sides.

solutions.reliable: Interior and exterior angles at a vertex add to 180, so each exterior angle is 30 degrees. Every polygon's exterior angles total 360, so the polygon has 360 / 30 = 12 sides. The transferable idea: switch to exterior angles, because their total never depends on the number of sides.
solutions.elegant: Turning once round the outside of the shape is one full revolution, and each corner turns 30 degrees, so there are twelve corners.

whyOnTest: The interior angle formula is the slow route and runs out of time; the exterior-angle total of 360 is the one fact that makes these instant.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
